nanopubs.returns: exit 0 and an empty `unexpected` list, or a FAIL line per record naming each unexpected issue
nanopubs.rule: Exit 0 with an empty `unexpected` list is the ONLY pass. Four issues are allowed by name on an unsigned draft: no signature, no assertion template, no provenance template, creation time older than one hour. Anything else fails.

nanopubs.returns: three fixtures: a bait record that must read valid, a truncated record that must read invalid, and a record whose own description forges an ISSUES: marker
nanopubs.rule: Run this before trusting a pass. A validator nobody has watched fail is one you cannot rely on; all three must PASS.

nanopubs.returns: LEAK lines for held-out claim ids and taxa, plus allowlisted warnings; exit 1 if any LEAK
nanopubs.rule: Run it over anything you are about to publish. Never allowlist a held-out id to make it pass - the allowlist is for files that filter the clade out.

leanbio.returns: every law with its id, version, status and lawset
leanbio.rule: Read the laws before designing, not after being refused.

leanbio.returns: a summary of violated / holds / out_of_scope / cannot_evaluate, then a verdict per law
leanbio.rule: Read `cannot_evaluate` first: each row names the input it would need. Supply it and call again, or report the absence. Do NOT substitute a default.

leanbio.returns: OK, or a FAIL naming the surface that is stale
leanbio.rule: A new law must reach the registry, the handlers, the static mirror, both CLIs, both MCP servers and the contract. This fails if any one is stale.

mcp.returns: every tool name, input schema and envelope shape
mcp.rule: Read the contract rather than guessing a tool name. There are 58 tools on the engine and 39 hosted.

mcp.returns: the claim IRI, its nanopub drafts and its fields, or {found:false} with the reason
mcp.rule: A malformed id answers {found:false} naming why, rather than throwing. Treat the refusal as information.

mcp.returns: 14 questions, each split into a formalisable core and an empirical remainder
mcp.rule: The split is the point: Lean can settle what follows from what, never what the world is like.

studio.call: node sim-engine/cli.mjs tool parse_design_text --json '{"text":"a zebrafish with large wing-like pectoral fins that can glide"}'
studio.returns: a spec with start_from, criteria in SI units, and the clauses it could NOT parse
studio.rule: Check the unparsed clauses before using the spec. They are reported, never silently dropped - on that input three of them are.

studio.returns: every part with its ontology id and whether its geometry is measured or schematic
studio.rule: A part marked schematic is a stand-in. Do not quote its dimensions as a measurement.

studio.returns: guides, donors, pegRNAs and an off-target table
studio.rule: A proposal for a wet lab to check, never a protocol. With NVIDIA_API_KEY set, Evo2 RANKS the options; it never gates them.

harness.returns: five named results, per_scale_coverage, a verdict with withheld_because, and a composite marked not-the-verdict
harness.rule: Never sum the five. Read per_scale_coverage BEFORE any result: a scale with no coverage has not passed, it has not been looked at.

harness.returns: the chosen functional analogue, both distances, and nearest_partial_analogues when nothing qualifies
harness.rule: The analogue is CURATED, not searched: a registry of four functions, first match in source order. No database is queried and no model is prompted. If no_analogue is true, nothing is substituted.

harness.returns: a gate string with the reachable launch speed against v_min, plus standing checks reported beside the gate
harness.rule: The gate text is the answer. On our own design it reads FAIL: 0.67 m/s against 8.64 m/s required.

harness.returns: a row per requirement: SAME, ALLELIC, PARALOGUE, ANALOGOUS_SET, COMPENSATORY or UNRESOLVED, plus coverage
harness.rule: Report the unassessable count. On our design 22 of 73 were assessable and 19 of those did not resolve.
